PLAN FACTS VERIFIED IN THE TREE — no defect found, and one CROSS-TICKET TRAP the implementer must
not walk into. Checked at 47b9a511871.

EVERYTHING THE PLAN ASSERTS IS TRUE:
 * adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py EXISTS (3.3K) and already holds LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA (:22)
   and LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA (:49), so the canonical home the plan names is real and the ticket-type

 * The J2 alias-import precedent is where the plan says, outbound_fields.py:35-36:
       from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY
       from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA  as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS
 * Both one-literal guards exist and are the shape to copy:
   test_exactly_one_status_map_literal_within_adapters (:296) and
   test_exactly_one_priority_map_literal_within_adapters (:306).

*** THE TRAP: USE AN ABSOLUTE IMPORT HERE, NOT A RELATIVE ONE — AND DO NOT CARRY THIS IDIOM OVER TO
cc77. ***
The J2 precedent's own comment states the reason for the absolute form, and it is load-bearing:
'this module is loaded via spec_from_file_location with NO PACKAGE CONTEXT in several tests, where a
RELATIVE IMPORT WOULD RAISE ImportError.' So copying J2 exactly — absolute — is correct for this
ticket, and 'tidying' it to a relative import would break test loading.

That sits in DIRECT TENSION with sibling ticket cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8, which established (and I
re-verified independently) that mypy WIDENS anything imported through the top-level
'rebar_reconciler.' name to Any, because that name is a runtime sys.path injection rather than an
importable distribution, and ignore_missing_imports is set globally. Both facts are true at once and
they do not conflict, because they are about DIFFERENT THINGS:
  * THIS ticket imports a DICT. Nothing is attribute-checked, so Any-widening costs nothing and the
    runtime import-form requirement (spec_from_file_location compatibility) wins. Absolute is right.
  * cc77 imports a TYPE used in ANNOTATIONS. There, Any-widening silently destroys the entire
    enforcement the ticket exists to add, so a resolvable (relative) import is mandatory.
Stating it here because the two tickets are in the same epic and an implementer who reads one and
then the other could plausibly 'unify the import style' and silently break either the tests (going
relative here) or the type enforcement (going absolute there). Neither is a style question.

Also already recorded on this ticket: the two _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE copies are CONTENT-IDENTICAL, so
the unification is behaviour-preserving and needs no divergence decision.

CI-INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE — a Verified -1 / Code-Review -1 pair appeared on patch set 2 of BOTH
changes that was NOT a test failure and NOT the pip-audit blocker. Recording the mechanism so the
next agent does not misread it as a real regression or re-do the work.

WHAT HAPPENED: runs 30772712323 (change 1240) and 30772713254 (change 1241) both ended
conclusion=CANCELLED, and in both the `build-and-test (gate + suite on the patchset)` job was
SKIPPED, not failed — `clear-vote` was cancelled early, so everything downstream skipped or
cancelled. The `vote` job runs `if: always()`, so it still cast Verified -1 (and Code-Review -1)
off a run that never executed a single test. A cancelled run is therefore INDISTINGUISHABLE from a
genuine failure by the vote alone; the run's job list has to be read to tell them apart.

WHY: .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:40-43 sets
    concurrency:
      group: gerrit-verify-${{ github.event.inputs.GERRIT_CHANGE_ID || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
The run history shows dispatches arriving in near-simultaneous PAIRS 1-2s apart, with the earlier
member of each pair killed when the next pair queues — i.e. under this session's multi-agent load
the group is not isolating per change the way the comment above it ("a newer patchset for the same
change cancels the in-flight run") intends. Consequence worth knowing: rechecking two stacked
changes in the same breath is self-defeating, and a recheck can also cancel ANOTHER agent's
in-flight run. Serialize rechecks on a stack; do not fire both at once. I did not touch the
workflow (out of scope, and it is a repo-wide condition, not this ticket's).

RESOLUTION: the stale votes were cleared automatically and a fresh run (30772783956) started on
its own — no further recheck was needed, and I deliberately did not post another one rather than
add to a contended queue and risk cancelling someone else's run.

REAL SIGNAL SO FAR: on the last run that actually executed the suite, the ONLY non-pip-audit
failure was the docs/env-vars.md drift gate, which patch set 2 fixes. Every other job was green:
lint + type-check, module-size gate, artifact provenance, golden-path clean install, both

compiled_state.description:
# Single-source the ticket-type map and extend the one-literal guard to cover it

## Context

This is the SAME defect class as the just-closed bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61, still live in a third
map — and the guard that was supposed to prevent recurrence does not cover it.

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` enforces "exactly one dict
literal defines each value map within `adapters/`" for the STATUS map
(`test_exactly_one_status_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:300`) and the PRIORITY map
(`test_exactly_one_priority_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:308`). There is no such
assertion for the TICKET-TYPE map, and it is duplicated:

* `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE: dict[str, str] = {...}`, read at
  `:129` for the Cloud create path.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": ...}`,
  read at `:61` for the DC create path.

Both were verified present in the tree. `config.py:11` also references a `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` in a
comment, which is worth checking for a third copy while doing this.

### Every consumer of the symbol, enumerated

A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search —
the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan
accounts for all of them:

1. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — definition (Cloud). Moves.
2. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:129` — Cloud create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
3. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — definition (DC). Moves.
4. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:61` — DC create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
5. `rebar_reconciler/config.py:11` — a COMMENT only, no literal. Confirms there is no third copy in
   config; the finding is recorded here so the check need not be repeated.
6. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:8` — a
   docstring mention. No code impact.
7. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:87` —
   **a live external consumer**: `assert "session_log" not in _of._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`, where `_of`
   is the `outbound_fields` module. This reads the name as a MODULE-LEVEL ATTRIBUTE on
   `outbound_fields`. If the relocation leaves the canonical map bound only under a new name (e.g.
   `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`) or referenced inline, this test breaks with `AttributeError`.

**Required binding strategy (this is not optional):** in `outbound_fields.py`, import the canonical
map under the historical private name, exactly as J2 did for the other two maps at
`outbound_fields.py:35-36`:

```python
from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE
```

That keeps `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` resolvable, so site 7 and the create-path read at
site 2 need no edit. The DC backend gets the same treatment for its own call site. If the
implementer instead chooses to rename, then site 7 MUST be updated in the same change and the suite
re-run to prove it — the choice is free, leaving site 7 broken is not.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The two copies are read by the two CREATE paths. A divergence means the same local ticket type
becomes a different Jira issue type depending on deployment — silently, at creation, with no
comparison anywhere that would notice. fe15's status map had already drifted by one key
(`"deleted"`) before anyone looked; there is no reason to assume this one is luckier, and nothing
would tell us.

## Approach

Follow the **J2** pattern (story 62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743), which is the established local idiom for a
map that lives on BOTH sides of the `adapters/` boundary and was reviewed when it landed: relocate
the single definition into `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` alongside `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` and
`LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`, have both create paths import it under an alias, then extend the boundary
guard so a future third copy fails the build.

Note explicitly that fe15 is NOT the precedent to copy for the mechanism, only for the defect class.
fe15 deliberately used a **parity test rather than a shared import**, because its third copy lived in
`rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a zero-dependency core module that must not import a vendor adapter
package. That constraint does not apply here: both copies of the TYPE map already live under
`adapters/`, so the shared import J2 used is available and is the right move.

**Compare the two copies BEFORE unifying them.** If they have already drifted, the unification is a
BEHAVIOUR change for one deployment and needs the divergence decided explicitly and recorded — the
way J2 decided `"deleted" -> "Done"` — not silently resolved by whichever copy is moved.

## Scope

- `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` — the single definition (and its export from the package
  `__init__`, matching how the status/priority maps are exposed).
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — delete the literal, import under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`
  alias.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — delete the literal, import under the same alias.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — extend the one-literal guard
  to the type map.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` — touched ONLY
  if the alias strategy above is not followed; unchanged if it is.
- the characterization pins for the type mapping on both create paths (see Testing) — **this ticket
  owns them unconditionally**.

## Testing

* the guard must FAIL when a second literal is reintroduced. "Mutation-checked" here means a
  concrete manual mutation, not a mutation-testing tool: re-add a literal
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": "Story", "bug": "Bug", "epic": "Epic"}` to
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, run the boundary-guard module, record that the new test is
  RED (and note the pass/fail counts), revert the mutation, record that it is GREEN again.
* both create paths keep producing their current issue-type values, pinned BY VALUE — an assertion
  on the built `"issuetype"` field for each of `task`/`story`/`bug`/`epic` through the Cloud create
  path and through the DC create path, not an assertion on the map's shape.
* `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` still passes unmodified (the alias check).
* the full `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` suite is green after the relocation.

Ownership note: sibling story cedc (DC backend characterization suite) also touches DC create-path
characterization. To remove the ambiguity, the type-mapping pins are **owned here**; cedc depends on
this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the two existing copies are DIFFED and the result is recorded in a comment on this ticket
- [ ] if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly with its rationale recorded,
      not defaulted to whichever copy was moved
- [ ] exactly one `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`-equivalent literal exists under `adapters/`, and it lives in
      `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`
- [ ] both create paths (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`)
      read that single definition, imported under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` alias
- [ ] `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` still resolves as a module attribute, proven by
      `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` passing UNMODIFIED — or, if the implementer
      renamed instead, that test is updated in the same change and passes
- [ ] the boundary guard covers the ticket-type map
- [ ] that guard is MUTATION-CHECKED by the concrete procedure in Testing, with the RED and GREEN
      verdicts recorded in a comment
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the Cloud create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the DC create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the `config.py:11` comment reference is checked for a backing third copy, and the finding is
      recorded either way

file_impact.reason: canonical home for the single ticket-type map literal, alongside LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA and LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA (J2 pattern)
remove the Cloud copy; import canonical map under the historical private alias _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE so the module-attribute consumer keeps resolving
remove the DC copy; same alias treatment for its create-path read
extend the one-literal boundary guard to cover the ticket-type map, matching the status and priority guards
